characterList.name: Woman

content_metadata.description: A step-by-step guide showing a woman training a horse for riding, focusing on desensitization techniques and basic control exercises.

qAndA.answer: She lunges the horse in both directions.
qAndA.question: What is the first thing the woman does with the horse?

qAndA.answer: She's desensitizing the horse to the rope while she's in the saddle.
qAndA.question: What is the woman doing when she flips the rope over the horse's head?

qAndA.answer: She's getting the horse used to her touch so it won't be a trigger when she mounts or dismounts.
qAndA.question: Why does the woman rub her leg on the horse's butt?

qAndA.answer: She's getting the horse used to her weight and to show it that she is in control.
qAndA.question: Why does the woman put her full weight in the stirrup and lean on the horse?

qAndA.answer: She says it was a windy day and they figured they may as well use him as a Leader, implying that she may not have needed one otherwise.
qAndA.question: Why does the woman say it's good that she has a Leader today?

scenes.title: Lunging the Horse

scenes.contextualRelevance: Relevant to desensitizing horses during training.

narrativeProgression.description: The woman stops lunging the horse and starts flapping the stirrups and getting the horse used to them.
She starts moving the saddle around on the horse's back.

scenes.thematicElements: The woman continues to train the horse, getting it used to the stirrups and the saddle moving on its back.
scenes.title: Desensitization with Stirrups

scenes.contextualRelevance: Relevant to fine-tuning control over the horse.

narrativeProgression.description: The woman flexes the horse's head in both directions.

scenes.thematicElements: The woman continues to train the horse, focusing on flexing its head and neck for control and desensitizing it to being touched on the head.
scenes.title: Flexing and Petting the Horse

characterInteraction.description: The woman is the primary trainer, working to get the horse used to her presence and movements. The Leader acts as an assistant, helping to control the horse's movement and keeping it calm.

scenes.contextualRelevance: Relevant to more advanced horse training techniques focusing on safety and control.

narrativeProgression.description: The woman starts hopping up and down next to the horse to get it used to her movements.
She puts her full weight in the stirrups and leans on the horse.
The woman hangs off the side of the horse as the Leader walks the horse around.
While the woman is in the saddle, she flips the lead rope over the horse's head to get it used to the rope around its face.
The woman starts moving the horse's hindquarters over, preparing to teach it an emergency stop.
The woman rubs her leg on the horse's butt to desensitize it to her touch.

scenes.thematicElements: The woman continues to train the horse, focusing on desensitizing it to her weight, movements, and touch. She also begins to work on basic control exercises.
scenes.title: Advanced Desensitization Techniques

climax.description: The woman starts moving the horse's hindquarters over, preparing to teach it an emergency stop.

storylines.description: The progression of training from lunging to more advanced desensitization and control exercises.

timecoded_text_to_speech.text: First thing I do is launch her both directions to make sure the saddle is not
pinching her anywhere and that she's okay with what I'm doing and get her in the
working frame of mind before I start getting ready to mount. Then I just start
flapping the stirrups, getting her used to that feeling and used to the sound. Move
the saddle back and forth, shift it around like you would do if you were in the
saddle and had to move it over and I flex her both directions to make sure she's
soft to the halter and that I have control over her head, kind of like a safety
check before I mount. Helps to get her attention on me as well. Do it both sides.
Then I just start hopping up and down beside her like I would do when I'm
getting ready to get on so that she's okay with this and not frightened when I
do it. Then I put my full weight in the actual stirrups and lean on the side
of her. This is a safe position for me to be in. Just in case something happens
I can step down really quick and have control. Then I just put my full weight on
the other side of her because honestly I'm awkward and I can't really get my
foot up there on a new cold so then I just walk around hanging off the side of
her. I can hop down really quickly if I need to and I did that for a couple of
laps before I actually went and got on her all the way. Then as I have a leader
here today I'm using him to get her used to me petting her all over while she's
moving around so that she's not frightened of that at all. She probably would
have been fine without a leader but with it being such a windy day we
figured we might as well. Then I'm just flipping the rope back and forth over her
head. This way I can do that when I want to flex her both directions I don't
actually have to get off and change where the rope is. I can just do it from the
saddle and it gets her desensitized to this kind of thing around her face. So it
doesn't have to be pretty at all. It doesn't have to be beautiful. It just
desensitizes her to it. Here I am riding her by myself without any help and now
I'm just getting her used to moving her hindquarters over. This would be the
beginnings of teaching her how to do an emergency stop and what it does is it
just gives me some control over her movement in case something goes wrong. This
is teaching her to move her body over when I apply leg pressure. She's pretty
sensitive so it doesn't take much and also getting her used to not overreacting
when I add pressure. Then I just practice getting on and off her quite a few
times here so that she knows to stand still while I mount and dismount. There's
nothing worse than a horse that walks off when you're doing those things. So I
spend quite a bit of time getting her accustomed to that.
Then I just rub my leg on her butt so that if I ever did touch her when I mount
her dismount that it's not a trigger for her.
